# Decision history — raw-autotune

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## raw-autotune.decision.agpl-boundary-and-dependency-direction

### Revision 1 — raw-autotune stays AGPL; the dependency arrow points at JPXL, never back

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.agpl-boundary-and-dependency-direction/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "src/api.rs"`, `path "src/encoder_hints.rs"`

raw-autotune stays AGPL-3.0-or-later. The dependency arrow across the three-project image pipeline runs one way only: raw-autotune may depend on JPXL, and JPXL must not depend on raw-autotune, link it, or copy any of its implementation.

JPXL (jpegXL-rs) stays MIT OR Apache-2.0 and defines its own MIT-licensed input structs for anything it receives from this side, authored independently rather than copied. raw-autotune adapts to that contract; JPXL does not adapt to raw-autotune's types.

openarc already links raw-autotune as a path dependency, so the combined openarc binary is AGPL-derived. That is accepted deliberately, not overlooked.

**Context.** jpegXL-rs recorded the constraint from its own side in docs/generated/CURRENT-STATE.md: because raw-autotune is AGPL-3.0-or-later while JPXL is MIT OR Apache-2.0, JPXL must not directly depend on or copy its implementation absent an explicit relicensing or legal decision, and should use an independently authored neutral input contract with adaptation on the raw-autotune side or a process/sidecar boundary. This record is that explicit decision, resolving the question rather than relicensing. It is what makes the encoder-hint handoff (encoder_hints::SpatialAqMap, api::RenderedRgb16Image's exif/icc/color_space) safe to build against: the bytes and the shapes cross the boundary, the code does not.

**Consequences.** - Nothing in src/encoder_hints.rs or src/api.rs may be copied into JPXL. JPXL re-declares equivalent structs under its own licence and this side adapts. - Anyone distributing openarc distributes an AGPL work and must offer corresponding source. - A future JPXL-side wish for a raw-autotune type is answered by re-declaring it there, never by vendoring.

## raw-autotune.decision.face-detection-is-off-by-default

### Revision 1 — Face detection is gated off: zero true positives, and nothing consumed the mask

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.face-detection-is-off-by-default/1` · scope `path "src/cli.rs"`, `path "src/scene.rs"`, `path "src/types.rs"`

The YuNet face detector does not run unless `--semantic-faces` (API: `RenderOptions::semantic_faces`) asks for it. `scene::FACE_DETECTION_DEFAULT` is false.

It is gated, not deleted. The model and its provenance stay prepared and pinned in models/manifest.json, and `RegionMasks::blank()` still seeds an empty `Face` plane, so a run with the detector off has the same sidecar shape as one with it on: one fewer entry in `models`, and a `Face` mask that stays blank.

**Context.** raw-autotune.assessment.scene-evidence-usefulness records the measurement: over the 74-image day/night/extreme-bright corpus the detector returned zero faces, and the corpus's only person response was a low-confidence false positive on a faucet still life, so face and person exposure policy and encoder ROI are unsupported. Nothing consumes the mask. No exposure policy reads it, no encoder hint layer maps it, and the semantic path is observational by construction. So running it spent an ONNX session per frame to produce an empty plane that nothing looked at. Deleting it would assert more than the evidence supports. The honest reading is "this detector, at this 512 px letterboxed proxy, on this corpus", not "faces cannot be found here" — a proxy that small is a plausible cause on its own. The flag preserves the option to re-open that without re-preparing a model.

**Consequences.** - `--semantic` is cheaper by one ONNX session per frame and loads one fewer graph. - A sidecar from a default `--semantic` run lists only the segmenter in `models`. Consumers keying off `models` length rather than role will see the difference; consumers reading `masks` will not, because the shape is unchanged. - Any future face work starts by re-examining the proxy size, not by re-enabling the flag and hoping.

## raw-autotune.decision.harmonic-highlight-is-automatic

### Revision 1 — The conservative harmonic estimator is the automatic highlight path

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.harmonic-highlight-is-automatic/1` · scope `path "src/api.rs"`, `path "src/cli.rs"`, `path "src/highlight.rs"`, `path "src/main.rs"`, `path "src/pipeline.rs"`, `path "src/raw_highlight.rs"`, `path "src/types.rs"`

Ship the visually accepted harmonic highlight estimator at reconstruction strength 1 as archive-auto-v4. Its post-demosaic chromaticity transport begins at the historical 75% area-support boundary and fades inward to full correction at 88%, so it does not enter the mixed leaf/sky band responsible for the rejected coloured gradient tendrils.

The current per-pixel estimator remains available through `--highlight-method current` as a compatibility control. Compression-aware highlight ratio exponent 0.6 and exact external lens profiles remain opt-in and are not part of this promotion. Human review of credible sky topology is authoritative over aggregate chroma metrics for future changes.

## raw-autotune.decision.highlight-desaturation-uses-peak-preserving-white-path

### Revision 1 — Highlight desaturation follows a peak-preserving path to white

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.highlight-desaturation-uses-peak-preserving-white-path/1` · scope `path "src/color.rs"`, `path "src/tone.rs"`

Apply highlight desaturation by continuously lifting lower display-linear RGB channels toward the brightest channel while leaving the brightest channel invariant. Keep the existing headroom cap before this mix and recompute the gamut-compression luminance anchor afterwards.

Controlled renders with highlight reconstruction disabled and with PPG, RCD, AMaZE, and Rawler demosaicing retain the same lavender/purple source colour. On `_DSC1289` only about 0.7% of the purple-mask pixels carry nonzero reconstruction uncertainty, so another reconstruction rule would target the wrong signal. A spatial neutralisation prototype created visible white halos.

Consequences: the existing global highlight shoulder reduces the adjacency contrast without semantic sky detection, spatial halos, or the darkening caused by contraction around luminance. Recorded colour is reduced rather than erased, and reconstruction remains governed by raw-domain clipping evidence.

## raw-autotune.decision.key-decisions

### Revision 1 — Key Decisions

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.key-decisions/1` · scope `all`

1. **Where the diagnostics live.** Advice says "inside the owned color path." Decision: add hooks in `src/color.rs:develop` (which calls `highlight::reconstruct` and owns the working→display matrix) to emit dumps before/after `highlight::reconstruct` and before/after `compress_gamut` in `src/tone.rs:282`. Alternative rejected: extending only `pipeline::dump_stage` (which sees `LinearImage` after develop) — it cannot see the pre-reconstruction camera-RGB buffer the advice specifies (items 1-4). Use a `--dump-stages` extension (or new `--dump-highlight-stages DIR`) that writes both the existing `LinearImage` baseline dumps and the new camera-RGB + gamut-stage PNGs, reusing `tone::render_baseline` with/without the working→display matrix consistently. Keep the "best effort, never fails the file" contract (`src/pipeline.rs:137`).

## raw-autotune.decision.near-whiteness-replaces-chromaticity-solve

### Revision 1 — Highlight continuity comes from a near-whiteness weight, not a chromaticity prior

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.near-whiteness-replaces-chromaticity-solve/1` · scope `path "src/highlight.rs"`, `path "src/synthetic.rs"`, `path "src/tone.rs"`

The neighbourhood-guided log-chromaticity reconstruction (`q` prior plus least-squares intensity solve `s*`) that ff74d3b landed is withdrawn. The `da23c5f` anchor rule is restored as the reconstruction, and the regime discontinuity it was meant to cure is removed instead by `highlight::near_whiteness` — the second-largest per-channel clip confidence — which drives the anchor width, the effective strength, and each channel's share of the lift. At its two ends the rule is exactly `da23c5f`, so every assertion of that commit holds verbatim.

The prior is not recoverable by tuning. Inside a large blown region there is no unclipped neighbour within any affordable radius, so `q` falls back to the frame's mean chromaticity — vegetation on a landscape — and the fully-clipped arm had no defined solve at all. Measured on `_DSC1283`, a fully-clipped sky pixel left reconstruction at camera `[255, 227, 255]`, about half the original white-balance cast, and the renderer's `1 - u*0.85` chroma cut then hid that cast by collapsing the pixel onto its tone-mapped luminance at sRGB 184 — darker than its less-clipped neighbours, which is the taupe-blob-with-posterized-edges defect.

Consequences: the chroma gate in `tone.rs` withholds the saturation boost (interpolating to `unboosted_scale`) rather than scaling chroma toward zero, because withholding an opinion cannot darken a pixel and imposing the opposite one can. ff74d3b's display-brightness proxy is removed as redundant with the raw-domain map. The Oklab perceptual gamut mapping from the same commit is kept — it was not implicated. Reconstruction is also no longer the dominant cost: the sequential O(W*H*r^2) neighbourhood scan is gone, `_DSC1283` renders in 2.3 s rather than 27 s.

## raw-autotune.decision.profile-experiments-remain-opt-in

### Revision 1 — Lens and compression-aware ratio experiments remain opt-in

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.profile-experiments-remain-opt-in/1` · scope `path "src/api.rs"`, `path "src/cli.rs"`, `path "src/lens.rs"`, `path "src/tone.rs"`, `path "src/types.rs"`

Keep highlight color/luminance ratio exponent 1.0 and embedded DNG lens correction as the unattended defaults. Exponent 0.6 and exact Lensfun distortion/TCA correction remain explicit experiments.

The current-renderer corpus gate for exponent 0.6 improved scalar measures: median sky green deficit, near-white share, and paired saturation ratio. Visual review overruled that promotion because the rendered skies were still not credible and contained colored gradient tendrils. These spatial/topological failures were not represented by the aggregate metrics. The archive-auto-v3 promotion was therefore rejected, and `--highlight-color-ratio-exponent 0.6` remains only a controlled comparison.

Harmonic highlight reconstruction is governed separately by `raw-autotune.decision.harmonic-highlight-is-automatic`; promoting that estimator does not promote the compression-ratio or exact-lens-profile experiments.

## raw-autotune.decision.scene-classifier-training-stack

### Revision 1 — Model A trains in PyTorch and ships as ONNX; Burn rejected for training

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.scene-classifier-training-stack/1` · scope `path "models/**"`, `path "tools/scene_models/**"`

Model A (the CamSDD 30-way scene/lighting classifier) is trained in PyTorch and shipped as ONNX through the existing lege-gpu path; Burn is rejected as the training stack. Deciding points: (1) Burn's headline benefit — retiring the ONNX runtime — is void because Model B (C5) ships as ONNX regardless, so Burn inference would add a second inference stack rather than remove one; (2) option asymmetry — Burn imports ONNX but cannot export it, so PyTorch training keeps both shipping paths open (lege-gpu now, burn-import later) while Burn training forecloses ONNX, which matters in a workflow that explicitly budgets for failed drafts and rewrites; (3) the workload is recipe experiments, where torchvision/AMP/pretrained-zoo iteration is near-mechanical and Burn requires hand-rolled augmentation before experiment one; (4) the >=94% accuracy gate is calibrated against Python-stack challenge results, and the repo's model tooling (export.py, prepare.py, report.py) is already PyTorch+ONNX shaped.

**Context.** research/LIGHTING_DETECTION_PLAN.md rev 2 section 3 assessed Burn as feasible with a bounded backbone menu and left the stack choice as a phase-3 decision, naming PyTorch->ONNX as the fallback. The deciding review was asked to determine which stack is actually better for this use.

**Consequences.** Training lives in tools/scene_models/train_camsdd.py inside a .venv-train PyTorch environment (BSD-licensed toolchain, irrelevant to AGPL shipping). ResNet-50 exports a clean lege-gpu op set. Burn remains available later as an inference-only consumer via ONNX import if a pure-Rust classifier path is ever wanted.

## raw-autotune.decision.scene-perception-uses-lege-gpu-prepared-graphs

### Revision 1 — Perception layer uses default lege-gpu prepared graphs

`proposed` · `@raw-autotune.decision.scene-perception-uses-lege-gpu-prepared-graphs/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "examples/probe-scene-model.rs"`, `path "models/**"`, `path "src/analyze.rs"`, `path "src/api.rs"`, `path "src/pipeline.rs"`, `path "src/preview.rs"`, `path "src/scene.rs"`, `path "src/types.rs"`, `path "tools/scene_models/**"` · topic `scene-perception`

Build a perception layer, not a Samsung-style exclusive scene enum. Gather YuNet,
a remappable lightweight segmenter, and a reparameterized MobileOne-S0 backbone,
and rewrite them into FP32 NCHW prepared ONNX graphs that lege-gpu can load.

lege-gpu and the model-integrity dependency are unconditional normal dependencies:
scene support is present in default and --no-default-features builds. --semantic is
the runtime opt-in for collecting evidence. Inference prefers the shared hardware
wgpu adapter, records the selected backend in model provenance, and falls back to
the deterministic CPU reference executor when no usable hardware executor exists.

Slice 1 records SceneEvidence and does not change rendering. Later slices apply
only bounded, confidence-weighted adjustments, with the legacy controller as the
no-confidence fallback.

**Context.** The earlier CPU-reference default reflected a Linux RTX 4060 Vulkan failure that is no longer present. The same Linux host can now select and execute both prepared scene graphs on the RTX 4060 through lege-gpu.

**Consequences.** All normal builds compile lege-gpu. Hardware inference is preferred at runtime and may have device-initialization cost; semantic inference remains observational and CPU fallback remains available for portability.

## raw-autotune.decision.slice-5-continuous-confidence-edge-semantics

### Revision 1 — Define Slice 5 continuous-confidence edge semantics

`active` · `@raw-autotune.decision.slice-5-continuous-confidence-edge-semantics/1` · scope `path "docs/STATUS.md"`, `path "src/api.rs"`, `path "src/cli.rs"`, `path "src/color.rs"`, `path "src/raw_highlight.rs"` · topic `raw-highlight-continuous-confidence-edge-semantics`

Keep continuous confidence authoritative wherever evidence exists, but bound evidence-free degeneracies explicitly: project only zero-data/floor-coupled chroma cells to the measured boundary hull; require an accepted colour-line fit for partial-cell luminance support; reserve domes and neutral fallback for all-channel hard clips; retain trust-weighted grid values with mean-confidence compatibility topology; apply every nonzero clip confidence continuously; define fractional strength as one blend of the complete full target while public spatial methods remain full-only; and treat HCHROMA as ablation-only with post-sharpen final-dump identity as the standing output check.

**Context.** The joint log-chromaticity review exposed seven ambiguous edge cases spanning evidence-free chroma, no-fit luminance, soft shoulders, split-green grid topology, sub-threshold application, fractional strength, and standing diagnostics.

**Consequences.** The production path retains no binary final-authority threshold. Pathological cells cannot import unsupported hue or luminance, fractional semantics are safe before future API exposure, and the documentation and regressions pin the deliberate compatibility boundaries.
